purpose: Pattern Lab Canva-font automation policy. Canva preserves premium fonts through approved master templates; OpenClaw automates source selection, text/photo replacement plans, QA, owner packets, and final approval gates.
font_control_rule: Exact Canva fonts must live in owner-approved master templates. Runtime automation may change text, image fills, size, weight, color, and style only where the plugin supports it, but must not claim deterministic font-family control.
production_output_rule: Production-ready thumbnail output uses Canva first when available. If Canva is blocked by quota, auth, export, paid/pro asset, or tool availability, an approved free fallback renderer may satisfy production readiness only after source-first QA, mobile readability, typography, intentionality, renderer provenance, and owner-review gates pass.
blocked_visual_elements: bare redaction bars without readable surrounding words
required_before_owner_approval: approved Canva template or Canva image-to-design/import result for every thumbnail candidate
Canva preview/contact sheet for every owner-review candidate
total_public_text_rule: Every thumbnail must include the city name and may use at most 5 non-city public words across MAIN_HOOK plus optional SUPPORT_LINE.
support_line_rule: Support line is optional. If present, it must be 2-4 words and must not push total non-city public words above 5.
production_renderer_rule: Canva plugin/templates remain the primary production renderer. When Canva is unavailable for a recorded blocker, Pattern Lab may route to an approved free fallback renderer. Local renderers are production-capable only after approved-renderer coverage, source-first, typography, mobile, and owner-packet gates pass.
local_renderer_boundary: Local renderers may create production fallback candidates only when Canva has a recorded blocker and the approved fallback production gate passes; otherwise they remain source prep, drafts, diagnostics, and QA fixtures.
